Way forward
NREL    |    3
Background
 Benchmarking the computational performance of software algorithms 
and hardware devices is an interdisciplinary practice.
 Advancements in optimization solvers, including the use of GPUs, have 
not been well quantified across a diverse set of problems.
 Current benchmarking solutions need to be adapted to the diverse 
range of renewable energy problems to study the efficient use of 
compute capabilities including accelerators.
NREL    |    4
Photo by Joe DelNero / NRELMotivation
Develop a user-friendly benchmarking tool to evaluate 
performance of optimization solvers in solving 
renewable energy problems on an HPC.
NREL    |    5
Objectives
 Develop a tool to benchmark renewable energy problems across a 
wide range of optimization solvers.
 Post-process and visualize benchmarking results for easy analysis.
 Utilize High-Performance Computing (HPC) resources to accelerate 
benchmarking speed and expand capacity.
 Support GPU-based optimization solvers.

Benchmarks
OptiBench has been evaluated with three benchmark suites of interest to 
renewable energy research.
 CUTEst: Constrained and unconstrained testing environment with safe 
threads
 PGlib-OPF: Power grid library for benchmarking optimal power flow 
algorithms.
 WaterTAP: Open-source water treatment model library
NREL    |    12
Post-processor
OptiBench’s post-processor visualizes 
benchmarking results using interactive 
and intuitive plots.
 Cumulative time plots
 Performance profiles
 Robustness pie plots
 Heat maps
 Scatter plots

Way forward
NREL    |    14
Demonstration
 NREL’s Kestrel HPC CPU nodes: HPE Cray EX system,  2 × 52 dual socket Intel Xeon 
Sapphire Rapids processor and 256 GB RAM.
 1 node with 104 tasks per node and Julia v1.10.0 was used for the benchmark run.
 Benchmark sizes:
• CUTEst: 1531 problems
• PGLib-OPF: 199 problems
• WaterTAP: 72 problems
 A total of 10 solver-linear solver combinations were compared in this section.
